sentence: This project studies which genes and cell states in coronary artery walls drive coronary artery disease, using single-cell profiling of artery tissue.
This project builds a tool that uses deep learning to turn medical images into models of blood flow and pressure for patient-specific cardiovascular research.
This project studies how a mutation in a nuclear receptor affects neurogenesis at the molecular, cellular and behavioral levels.
This project tries to find out how thrombin links steatosis, inflammation and coagulation to hepatic fibrosis.
This project uses MRI to track how blood-brain barrier permeability and brain microstructure change during anti-amyloid immunotherapy for Alzheimer's disease.
This project studies how cancer cells, immune cells and stroma cells interact and communicate in the tumor microenvironment.
This project studies how cancer cells communicate with supporting cells in the tumor microenvironment of oral squamous cell carcinoma.
This project provides data management and statistical support to researchers studying balance and mobility in aging.
This project uses MRI and CT imaging to assess how tumors respond to treatment in cancer therapy trials.
This project provides resources to innovators who create pediatric medical devices that improve healthcare for children.
This project studies how plasma membrane abundance helps myeloid cells decide between migration, phagocytosis and NETosis.
This project combines quantitative genetics, experimental methods and clinical samples to study how genetic effects act from thymus development to immune-mediated disease.
This project studies how dosage-sensitive gene regulators change chromatin structure and spatial tissue organization in heart development in Down syndrome.
This project studies how lymphatic vascular niches control cancer stem cell plasticity as squamous cell carcinoma begins and progresses.
This project sets up research cores and projects to study cardiometabolic and mental health outcomes in US Asians.
This project compares the toll-like receptor 4 pathway in the blood and brain of people with depression and healthy participants.
This project tries to find out how mutations in a gene help drive acute lymphoblastic leukemia to start and progress in relapsed cases.
This project builds a method that lets a drug quickly switch on protein production in the body with low leakiness.
This project builds a 3D in silico model of mouse embryogenesis using single-cell spatial multi-omics and machine learning.
This project studies how electrical synapses shape brain oscillations during sleep and wakefulness and sensory processing.
